articles.title: World and European champion Spain loses first match since 2024 after 3-2 home defeat to England
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — World Cup winner Spain was beaten for the first time in more than two years after losing 3-2 at home to England in the Nations League on Sunday...
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — World Cup winner Spain was beaten for the first time in more than two years after losing 3-2 at home to England in the Nations League on Sunday.

Spain's 43-game unbeaten streak ended with a first defeat since a 1-0 loss to Colombia in March 2024 in a friendly match played at Wembley Stadium in London.

A few months later Spain won the European Championship and followed up that triumph with the World Cup earlier this year.

Although Spain lost the previous Nations League final to Portugal last year in a penalty shootout, that match counted as a draw statistically because it ended 2-2 after extra time . ___

articles.title: After 73-7 loss to hapless Washington State, Jim Mora Jr. says there are people at Colorado State 'that don't know how to win'
articles.summary: Mora's team has allowed 137 points over its last two games.
articles.body:
Jim Mora Jr. has been a very frustrated man in his first season at Colorado State. And after his team was absolutely shellacked by Washington State on Saturday night, he said he didn't think people at Colorado State know how to win.

Washington State beat Colorado State 73-7 as the Cougars ran for nine touchdowns. Washington State rushed 58 times for 535 yards; that's over nine yards a carry. Quarterback Owen Eshelman threw for a TD himself and was 13-of-14 passing for 135 yards. He barely averaged more yards per pass than the team did per rush.

The loss dropped Colorado State to 3-7 overall as the Rams have lost seven of their past eight games. Mora, who was hired from UConn at the end of the 2025 season, ended his postgame news conference saying that he thought his team would keep fighting over the last two games of the season. And then had this to say:

"Hopefully we can get a couple of wins, so they can learn how to win — what it takes to win," Mora said. "You know? I think that's a real problem here. And it has been for many, many years. These are people here that don't know how to win. The place I'd came from, they'd won 16 national championships in basketball so the whole school knew how to win. We gotta teach people around here how to win."

Colorado State, which went 2-10 a season ago after firing Jay Norvell seven games into the season, won eight games in 2024. Before that, the Rams had six straight losing seasons but won 10 games as recently as 2014.

UConn, meanwhile, has been proof that success in men's and women's basketball doesn't guarantee anything in football. While Mora led the program to back-to-back nine-win seasons in 2024 and 2025, UConn had 12 straight losing seasons before then. And over the 2018, 2019 and 2021 seasons — UConn didn't play football in 2020 — the Huskies were a combined 4-32 ahead of Mora's hire.

From this vantage point, the easiest way for Colorado State to start winning would be to start giving up fewer points. Yes, that sounds incredibly basic, but the Rams defensive statistics are absolutely preposterous this season.

Colorado State is giving up nearly 48 points per game and has allowed 137 points over its past two losses. The Rams are dead last among 138 FBS teams in scoring defense. Southern Miss is 137th with 36.5 points per game allowed. The Golden Eagles are closer to SMU, the team 79th in scoring defense, than they are to Colorado State one spot behind them.

Summers, the team's interim coach at the end of 2025, left the sideline in the middle of Oregon State's 56-26 win over the Rams on Oct. 3. After the game, Mora said that Summers was no longer with the program.

Since Summers' firing, Colorado State has allowed at least 64 points three times.

articles.title: De la Fuente: "¿Ahora qué pasa? Pues no pasa nada, que empieza un nuevo reto en marzo"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente acaba de pasar po la sala de prensa del estadio Metropolitano para ofrecer la última rueda de este histórico 2026, el año de la segunda estrella. La derrota: "Ha sido muy disputado ante un equipo muy enérgico. Nos ha costado. Nos ha faltado pausa. Pero hemos tenido muchas ocasiones. Estoy convencido de que lo mejor está por llegar. Orgullo de ser el seleccionador de este equipo. Les he dicho que esto sigue, que en marzo estamos en cuartos; hemos quedado segundos de grupo y estamos en cuartos, y tenemos todas las posibilidades de nuevo de ganar la Nations, y a eso vamos: a intentar ganarla de nuevo. No era fácil lo que habíamos hecho en el pasado, y hoy han demostrado los grandes jugadores que son y el gran equipo que forman. Es verdad que nosotros no hemos estado finos en esa media hora, pero al final siempre es lo mismo: ¿por qué no estás fino? Porque no estás fino tú o porque el rival es superior. Hoy, en esa primera media hora especialmente, creo que los otros quince minutos el partido se ha igualado bastante, y en el inicio del segundo tiempo, bueno, pues ha habido bastantes alternativas. Luego ya, desde que se han quedado con diez, hemos tenido la sensación de que podíamos dar la vuelta al marcador. Hay que saber ganar y saber perder. Hoy nos hemos encontrado ante una grandísima selección que lo único que hace es poner otra vez en valor todo lo que hemos hecho hasta ahora, porque a esta selección también le hemos ganado en otras ocasiones". Tuchel: "Con el seleccionador inglés no hay ningún problema, todo es admiración y respeto, muchísimo. Es verdad que cuando no estás acostumbrado a perder, llega un momento en que tienes un bajonazo y piensas: "Uf, pero ¿qué ha pasado?". Pues bueno, pero enseguida echas la vista atrás y dices: "Pero vamos a ver, ¿qué es lo que hemos transmitido a los jugadores y al equipo? Llevamos tres años sin perder, ganando la Eurocopa, la Nations League... sé que no es fácil, pero insisto, es por poner en contexto lo que sucede". Orgulloso de este equipo y del recorrido. ¿Ahora qué pasa? Pues no pasa nada. La pena es que no tenemos otra competición la semana que viene o dentro de diez días; ahora ya hay que esperar hasta marzo. Pues en marzo volveremos con los bríos renovados, pensando en superar la eliminatoria, plantándonos de nuevo en la final de la Nations e intentando ganarla. Sabiendo otra vez lo difícil que es volver a repetir éxitos de ese calibre, pero el espíritu, la intención y la ambición seguro que van por ahí". Cambios: "Por encima de 1,95 m, sufrimos mucho, y ya sabíamos de su envergadura, como hemos visto. El equipo inglés sí que es poderoso en este tipo de situaciones. Queríamos minimizar esas circunstancias con Zubimendi y Mikel Merino, que además son muy fuertes también en el juego aéreo, buscando primero tener cubierto ese aspecto. Además, Zubimendi y Mikel Merino, entre otros jugadores, son futbolistas excepcionales y fantásticos. No vamos a pensar que les estábamos haciendo ningún favor; se lo han ganado ellos. Son geniales en lo futbolístico porque son de los mejores del mundo en su posición. Eso es lo que pretendíamos, y luego, con los cambios y con que se han quedado con diez —cuando íbamos perdiendo—, lo que queríamos era quemar todas las naves e ir a por el rival, como hemos ido claramente, metiéndoles en su área y generando muchas ocasiones de gol. Se han generado, pero es verdad que también el portero rival ha tenido una actuación fantástica y ha evitado, sobre todo en los últimos cinco o diez minutos, dos o tres goles que podíamos haber materializado. En cualquier caso, ha sido un partido con muchas alternativas, pero destaco y pongo en valor al fantástico rival que nos hemos encontrado". Bajón: ¿Que si hemos bajado un peldaño? No lo creo, en absoluto. Venimos de competir al máximo nivel en escenarios complejísimos y contra rivales de una entidad enorme. Lo que pasa es que nos hemos acostumbrado tanto a ganar que cualquier bache o media hora menos brillante parece una catástrofe, pero esto es fútbol de élite. El otro día ante la República Checa y hoy en tramos de este partido nos ha costado más, es evidente, y hay que darle mérito al rival. Hemos vivido una semana peculiar, con exigencias máximas, pero el equipo ha dado la cara en todo momento. Lejos de bajar ningún peldaño, lo que hace esta derrota es poner aún más en valor todo lo que hemos conseguido hasta ahora. No se puede ganar siempre, por mucho que hayamos puesto el listón muy alto con tres años sin perder y levantando títulos. El espíritu, la ambición y la confianza en este grupo siguen intactos de cara a lo que viene en marzo. El privilegio, insisto, es tener a todas estas futbolistas maravillosas que nos han traído hasta donde nos han traído hasta ahora, y todavía, insisto, hay muchas cosas por hacer". La energía de Inglaterra: "Yo creo que este Inglaterra siempre se aplica con mucha energía, tiene mucho talento y futbolistas que, en lo colectivo, son muy buenas, pero en lo individual tienen un poder físico fantástico, a las que hemos sido capaces de doblegar en otras circunstancias. Pero en alguna ocasión también tienen que demostrar ellos habitualmente el potencial futbolístico que tienen. Yo creo que, aun así, todo el mundo quiere ganar a España; eso es una buena noticia, pero nosotros estamos preparados para superar esos retos. Quizás hoy, vuelvo a decir, nos quede ese sabor agridulce porque no estamos acostumbrados a esto, pero esto puede pasar. Era un partido que bien podría ser la final de un campeonato del mundo o de un campeonato de Europa, y en este tipo de encuentros, o estás muy fino y demuestras que tienes el nivel top, o el rival —Inglaterra, Francia, Italia, Portugal— te pasa por encima. Como hemos hecho otras veces nosotros, pues en esta ocasión Inglaterra —vuelvo a decir, hay que saber reconocerlo— ha sido superior gran parte del partido. Pero, aun así, creo que hemos tenido muchas opciones de darle la vuelta al resultado". Lo que viene: "Me gustaría estar la semana que viene con todos los jugadores de nuevo para recordarles lo difícil que es hacer lo que han hecho. Es lo que les he dicho en el vestuario, porque la verdad es que allí la gente estaba triste. Pero les he dicho: "Señores, ¿sabéis lo que habéis hecho? ¿Sabéis dónde estamos y lo que hemos conseguido? Entonces, pongamos en valor eso". Me gustaría estar la semana que viene con ellos para decirles de verdad, para decirles simplemente: "Esta es la realidad, chicos. Esto y esta dificultad es la que hemos tenido siempre, pero nos ha tocado ganar casi siempre". Ahora, esto es poner los pies en el suelo y valorar lo difícil que ha sido todo lo que se ha conseguido. Por eso echo de menos otra concentración ya para decirles esto, pero en lo demás seguís siendo como somos, con la actitud que tenemos, con la sensación de equipo, la familia que siempre me gusta utilizar. El equipo está tremendamente motivado para empezar un nuevo reto, y eso es lo que esperamos".

articles.title: Champion of Champions snooker results: Kyren Wilson wins third straight title with win over Chris Wakelin
articles.summary: Kyren Wilson survives a stunning late comeback from Chris Wakelin to win the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester.
articles.body:
Kyren Wilson survived a stunning late comeback from Chris Wakelin to win the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester.

Wilson, 34, looked to be cruising to victory with a 9-3 lead and needed just one more frame for victory, but a determined Wakelin fought back in the evening session to put himself in touching distance at 9-8.

Wakelin's impressive breaks of 131, 57 and 50 put Wilson on notice but he held his nerve for a 10-8 win with his fourth century break of the day.

The win extends Wilson's fine run of form as he sealed his third consecutive title after triumphs at the Northern Ireland Open and the International Championship .

He started confidently, taking control with a 135 break in the opening frame, and surged into a 4-0 lead before Wakelin recovered to make it 4-3.

Wilson then notched five frames in a row and had the title in his sights before Wakelin started his response to set up the thrilling finale.

"I made hard work of that in the end, didn't I?" Wilson told ITV after his victory.

"Full respect to Chris, he really dug in there well. I played some good stuff and felt I had killed the match in the first session.

"I've never felt so exhausted, I'm so drained. I felt so much pressure to get over the line."

It is Wilson's first Champion of Champions win, having previously reached the final in 2018 where he lost to seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan.

He is also the first player to win three tournaments in a row since Judd Trump in 2023.

articles.title: Tennessee WR Mike Matthews likely out for rest of 2026 season after knee injury vs. Texas A&M
articles.summary: Matthews is the only Tennessee player with more than 350 receiving yards.
articles.body:
No. 8 Tennessee is set to play the rest of the season without its top wide receiver.

According to On3, Mike Matthews is likely out for the remainder of 2026 following a knee injury suffered in the Volunteers' 22-7 win over Texas A&M. Matthews was on crutches on the sideline after the injury, which came after he had two catches for 42 yards.

Matthews is second on the team with 39 catches. Only Braylon Staley, with 40, has more. But Matthews is the only player with over 500 receiving yards, leading the team with 608 yards and four touchdowns. Staley has 343 yards, and no other Vol has more than 200.

Every other Tennessee player has combined to catch seven touchdowns.

In 2025, Matthews had 53 catches for 813 yards and four scores over 13 games. He could be an early-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, though the late-season injury may open the door further for a return to Knoxville.

Matthews' absence is a huge loss for an offense that's having to lean on the run game as much as it can. George MacIntyre has been Tennessee's starter, but he was replaced by Week 1 starter Faizon Brandon because of a knee injury in the second half of the win over the Aggies.

Through 10 games, Brandon and MacIntyre have combined to go 154-of-237 passing for 1,688 yards and 11 touchdowns with four interceptions. Both are averaging around seven yards per pass attempt.

Tennessee has a clear path to the College Football Playoff with wins over LSU and Vanderbilt in the final two weeks of the regular season. And if more teams ahead of them lose games, Tennessee could even be positioned to host a home playoff game.

articles.title: Spain 2-3 England: Three Lions produce best win under Thomas Tuchel
articles.summary: England's stunning win in Spain had everything - and was their best under Thomas Tuchel, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel went with bold words when reminded about the caution that sabotaged England's World Cup hopes and left them with so much to prove against Spain in the Nations League on Sunday.

In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions.

Tuchel looked his inquisitors in the eyes and declared: "We are up for something spectacular."

To say Tuchel and England kept their word was a masterpiece of under-statement after the finest night of the head coach's reign resulted in a 3-2 victory that was large parts magnificent, some parts madness - and all parts spectacular.

It also ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run - setting aside their penalty shootout defeat by Portugal in the 2025 Nations Cup final.

If England and Tuchel could be accused of being cowed by pressure when they led Argentina in the ill-fated World Cup semi-final, they were thrillingly positive in this unforgiving Madrid environment.

The question being asked when England held a one-goal advantage through Harry Kane's penalty at half-time was 'what would theirs and Tuchel's reaction be?' Stick or twist?

Would Tuchel tell England to press their foot on the pedal for acceleration? Or would he take the approach of going into reverse gear, as he did to ill-fated effect against Argentina?

How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

Who swaggered around like he owned the place? Spain v England ratings

England hold on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

The answer was delivered when they added goals from Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White in the first 12 minutes of the second half.

This being England, they then created a mess for themselves when Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the area after 65 minutes, although the main culprit was Jarell Quansah for initially conceding possession.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the spot and, when Yamal set up Nico Williams for Spain's second with 15 minutes left, it looked like more than an hour of faultless England football might be wasted.

But not a bit of it, as goalkeeper James Trafford produced heroics and England defended with every fibre to close out this landmark win.

Was this the statement victory that was almost demanded of Tuchel as recompense for the World Cup disappointment, a performance to convince the doubters?

"We're fully aware what we put out there," said Tuchel afterwards. "What a performance we put out for 65 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course, the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and the characteristics of the game... but we know, and the players know very, very well, what they put out there. That is the statement - and that is the significance of this victory."

Simple details of the game barely touch the sides of a night filled with quality and glorious chaos, vindication for Tuchel and England's positive approach.

Spain opened with an ostentatious parade of the World Cup in front of England's players as the teams lined up, perhaps a psychological reminder of the superiority that has seen them dominate international football.

What followed, at times literally, reduced Spain's supporters to stunned silence and their players to a shell-shocked shambles chasing the shadows that were overpowering them.

England's white shirts were everywhere but Spain could not get near them. The tormentors had become the tormented.

It was alien territory for a Spain side that has carried all before them, while England's fans tucked away high in a corner of this vast arena were equally unbelieving as a dream unfolded in front of them.

England, for 65 minutes, were in a different class to Spain. And, yes, you have read that right.

From the first whistle, employing a suffocatingly high press, England ran all over Spain.

When White crowned a superb move with the third goal four minutes after Konsa's second, it looked, remarkably, to be a case of how big England's victory margin would be.

In the end, the margin was narrow but the stature and significance of England's victory was huge.

Tuchel labelled this meeting with Spain as "proof of concept at the highest level".

There was no doubt the German manager and England were under fierce scrutiny after the manner of the collapse, mentally and tactically, against Argentina at the World Cup.

Here they delivered the proof they can match the best then beat them.

If the vital signs were being forensically examined for evidence Tuchel has learned lessons from a chastening World Cup, that England have improved after that harrowing experience, this game delivered these conclusions.

Of course, England must do it again. Do it when the pressure and expectation in at its highest.

The Nations League is competitive but cannot be compared to a World Cup and European Championship, both titles currently in the possession of the team they beat here.

But England's world-class players delivered - Kane inevitably with his 93rd international goal, but Jude Bellingham was on a level of his own, the outstanding performer on both sides with an individual display simply confirming he is the player with everything.

And Tuchel got his big calls right, especially selecting Trafford, who responded superbly in a frantic closing phase. White, making a strong claim for the right-back berth, not only scored a goal but produced crucial challenges in the face of relentless, albeit belated, Spain pressure.

"This was the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness," said Tuchel. "It was on the highest level football wise in all aspects of the game. We did everything that needs to be done together.

"The deep build-up. The high press. The counter-attack. The tracking. The defensive phases. This was an excellent performance and of course a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

"We overcame some difficult moments in the end. That's how it is. But we are very well aware which steps we took now through after the World Cup."

England's win means they top their Nations League group, but the importance spreads much wider than simply a league table.

The first 65 minutes were simply breathtaking. Spain wilting under attack after attack. Spain rattled until they shook as England refused to allow them meaningful possession.

After Anderson's dismissal, bad memories were revisited as England were forced into a rearguard action, but any other result than the one that was eventually delivered would have been a huge injustice.

England survived 29 nervous minutes, including added time, to make a powerful statement about their current status, which is much healthier than when recriminations about Tuchel's approach provided the post-World Cup narrative.

"I'm very impressed with the steps that we took after the World Cup", said Tuchel. "We wanted to get better, better in a deep build-up, get better in defending in a low block and, on top of it, we wanted always to impose our identity and the way we want to play against every opponent.

"I think this was clearly visible throughout the whole group phase. The results followed with an excellent group phase."

Was this the finest performance of Tuchel's time in charge? Most observers felt so, but the head coach was best placed to answer.

"Yes, given the circumstances," he said, "and the pressure, the quality, where we played in this building against the reigning world champions, unbeaten in 43 matches. Putting a performance out there in Madrid, and in this environment, was a very complete performance."

Tuchel will, of course, need repeat performances - but the outstanding ability and character England displayed here to beat the World Cup holders will deliver a huge injection of confidence and self-belief.

articles.title: Spain 2-3 England: How did Thomas Tuchel's side win and what was learned from Argentina defeat?
articles.summary: Trying to protect a lead in the closing stages, England have been here before - so how did they cling on against Spain?
articles.body:
England held on to beat Spain 3-2 with a backs-to-the-wall finale in the Nations League to finish top of their group.

But many observers would have been feeling a sense of deja vu from the World Cup semi-final when England sat back and were beaten by Argentina .

So what was different this time? BBC Sport has a look.

First of all the context of the two games was entirely different.

England were 1-0 up against Argentina in the 55th minute on neutral territory in Atlanta - and still had all their players.

Anthony Gordon had put them ahead but Lionel Messi set up Enzo Fernandez and then Lautaro Martinez late on.

But against Spain the best performance of Thomas Tuchel's reign had them 3-0 up through goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Elliot Anderson then fouled Lamine Yamal for a penalty, which Mikel Oyarzabal scored - and that began the siege at a partisan Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Nico Williams made it 3-2 but Spain could not find an equaliser, thanks in part to England keeper James Trafford.

"Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]," Tuchel told ITV afterwards. "That's the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners."

60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages

England cling on to stun world champions Spain in thriller

Making defensive subs is fine when it works - but when it does not, boy will a manager hear about it.

In the World Cup last 16, England had been 2-1 up against Mexico in the Azteca when Jarell Quansah was sent off.

Tuchel brought on three defenders for a defender, a midfielder and a forward.

But England won 3-2 and Dan Burn's cameo was the stuff of legend.

However, nine days later with England 1-0 up against Argentina, Tuchel did the same again - three defenders on for a defender, midfielder and forward.

The first of those subs, with Konsa replacing Anthony Gordon, was in the 72nd minute.

And England just sat back until Argentina broke their resistance.

However, against Spain this time, despite England being down to 10 men and facing incessant pressure, Tuchel was not so quick with defensive subs.

Myles Lewis-Skelly, replacing Harry Kane, was the first on after 78 minutes - 15 minutes after Anderson's sending off. And then five minutes later he brought on two more players - but one of them was a striker in Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Burn replaced fellow defender White in the 89th minute.

"Harry played 78 minutes, Jude [Bellingham] 83 minutes and then just defending and defending, it's tiring," explained Tuchel.

"So we needed fresh energy. I was asked yesterday what happens if there needs to be a critical or crucial substitution. And I said, I feel free enough to take any substitution if I think it is necessary to help the team and to influence the game.

"I feel free enough to do that and I think there was a lot of defending needed. So we just went for some fresh legs."

England actually faced more of a siege this time than against the Argentines, the stats confirm.

In the final 30 minutes they faced 19 shots from Spain, with seven on target and an expected goals (xG) total of 2.53.

Argentina, in that time, had 10 shots, with four on target and an xG of 1.41.

In terms of passes from England the numbers were similar with 65 against Argentina and 61 against Spain - both times with an accuracy rate of about 64%.

In Thursday's 2-1 win against Croatia , as a comparison, they tried 557 passes with accuracy of 89%.

"For half an hour it was Mexico reloaded and it felt like we were back in the Azteca. We had to overcome 30 minutes which, against Spain, felt like three hours," Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"The difficult thing is it's not only a red card, it's a red card, and a goal so that makes a completely new game. Thirty minutes against the world champion feels like three hours. I said it before in the stadium and wave after wave after wave."

England were criticised for blowing a 2-1 half-time lead at Wembley in their first Nations League game with Spain .

But on that day their final 30-minute figurers were much better - with only five shots faced and 176 attempted passes with a 90% accuracy.

So what was different this time? Perhaps the team showed more resilience and unity?

After Spain had pulled one back England's players had a huddle.

"I love the fact the team went into a huddle and if anything the manager's stepped back because he wants to see the player reaction," said ex-England defender Matt Upson on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I almost think that the trauma from that sending off of Elliot Anderson has almost been a positive thing for England because it's given the team a chance to get together and cope in what is an incredibly difficult situation and come through the other side.

"There was so much going on in this game. England had to suffer and came through the other side."

Defender and goalscorer White was asked about the huddle after the game.

"Just stay calm, when you're one down it becomes more difficult and things change so it was all about managing that," he said.

Another factor was the performance of England keeper James Trafford, who made six saves - with four of them coming in the final 12 minutes of the game with the score at 3-2.

He made an incredible double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Lamine Yamal in injury time.

Upson said: "I think that double save was the moment for Spain and Trafford had the answers."

articles.title: El florecer de Damsgaard: la revelación de la Euro’21 recoge el testigo de Eriksen
articles.standfirst: El mediapunta del Brentford, que ha generado cuatro goles en esta Nations League, se ha erigido en el líder futbolístico de Dinamarca
articles.summary: El mediapunta del Brentford, que ha generado cuatro goles en esta Nations League, se ha erigido en el líder futbolístico de Dinamarca
articles.body: No todos los futbolistas siguen el mismo proceso de evolución. Mikkel Damsgaard (Jyllinge, 2000) puede dar buena fe de ello. Con apenas 21 años, maravilló con Dinamarca llegando a las semifinales de la Eurocopa 2021. Más de cinco años después, ya con 26 y en plena madurez futbolística, ya se siente en disposición de recoger el testigo de Christian Eriksen. Formado en el Nordsjaelland, la mejor escuela del fútbol danés, dio el salto a la Sampdoria en el verano de 2020 por cerca de siete millones de euros. Semanas más tarde, Kasper Hjulmand le dio la oportunidad de debutar con Dinamarca —fue titular y asistió contra Suecia— para, al finalizar aquella temporada, ser uno de los 23 elegidos que acudirían a la Eurocopa 2021. “Su cabeza va uno a dos segundos más rápido que la del resto. Consigue que parezca que haya un poco más de tiempo. Une las jugadas y crea ocasiones con sus pequeños pases. Cuando crezca un poco y gane más intensidad, veremos un jugador de élite”, ya advertía un Kasper Hjulmand que le dio paso en el once tras dejarle sin jugar en el debut ante Finlandia… para terminar erigiéndose en la gran revelación de aquella Euro. De vuelta a la Sampdoria, apenas pudo disputar 12 partidos en la temporada 21-22 a causa de unos problemas musculares que le tuvieron durante 186 días apartado de los terrenos de juego. Sin embargo, el recuerdo que dejó en la Eurocopa seguía latente y, aquel verano, Thomas Frank se lo llevó por 15 millones para su Brentford como sustituto, precisamente, de Eriksen. “Después de hablar con Thomas (Frank) sobre cómo le gusta jugar a él y cómo yo me siento cómodo, sentí que era un ‘match’ perfecto”, reconoció en su presentación. “Conozco a alguno de los compañeros desde hace mucho tiempo. Es agradable entrar en un vestuario nuevo y ver caras familiares”. La adaptación a la Premier League no fue sencilla. En una liga tan física, no es un mediapunta que destaque por su velocidad o facilidad para ganar duelos. Poco a poco, sin dejar de lado su esencia para flotar entre líneas y filtrar pases, logró ir haciéndose al campeonato… hasta convertirse en uno de los grandes referentes de un Brentford que lleva años llamando a la puerta de Europa. “Hay muchas cosas en las que he estado trabajando, pero es más una cuestión de mentalidad y confianza”, explicaba el pasado enero de 2025, tras renovar hasta 2030, un Mikkel Damsgaard que puede presumir de ser el centrocampista de la Premier League que más ocasiones crea por partido (2.74); el segundo que más pases clave (1.83) reparte; y el segundo que más regates completa (1.6). Dinamarca, ahora con Brian Riemer en el banquillo, también está empezando a sacar provecho de esta versión después de quedar apeada del pasado Mundial en la pasada ‘repesca’. El puesto de ‘10’ es suyo y es el verdadero ‘cerebro’ del equipo. Así lo reivindicó en la goleada a Portugal: 49 toques; 35/41 pases; tres pases clave; dos faltas recibidas; y 4/4 duelos ganados. Sirvió, además, la asistencia del 0-2 para Hojlund con un envío exquisito al segundo palo para elevar a cuatro los goles que ha generado en esta Nations League. “Siento que, cada vez, mi rol es más grande. Hace poco, alguien me dijo que estaba entre los cinco jugadores actuales de la selección con más partidos. Asumo la responsabilidad”, reconocía Damsgaard recientemente. Ha pasado un lustro. Pero merecía la pena tener paciencia con la revelación de la Euro’21.

articles.title: Jorge Jesus se entrega a Joao Félix: “Me dio confianza para sacar lo mejor de mí”
articles.standfirst: Su posición como ‘10’ evidencia su intención de convertirle en la nueva estrella de Portugal tras el adiós de Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.summary: Su posición como ‘10’ evidencia su intención de convertirle en la nueva estrella de Portugal tras el adiós de Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.body: El adiós de Cristiano Ronaldo ha creado una necesidad de la que Portugal llevaba 23 años despreocupada: encontrar un nuevo símbolo al que aferrarse. Jorge Jesus acaba de dar comienzo a esa búsqueda… y la sensación que transmite es que su primera intención es entregarle las llaves de la ‘seleçao’ a Joao Félix (Viseu, 1999). Le conoce a la perfección. De hecho, Jorge Jesus, seguramente, sea el entrenador que haya logrado exprimir la mejor versión de Joao Félix a lo largo de una carrera que le ha llevado por Benfica, Atlético de Madrid, Barcelona, Chelsea y Milan hasta acabar recalando en Al Nassr. Juntos, levantaron la pasada Saudi Pro League y, con 34 goles producidos en las 33 jornadas que disputó, el ‘menino de ouro’ fue elegido como MVP del campeonato. “Llego más confiado que nunca. Ha sido un año increíble. Principalmente, ya vengo diciéndolo desde hace mucho tiempo, he podido jugar en mi posición natural, que es donde me siento más cómodo. Jorge Jesus se dio cuenta de eso. Me dio confianza para sacar lo mejor de mí”, llegó a reconocer Joao Félix durante la disputa del pasado Mundial. Jorge Jesus, por su parte, mostró sus cartas nada más asumir el mando de la selección. “Joao Félix tiene unas características que encajan dentro de mi idea de juego. No jugará de extremo, lo que no quiere decir que, esporádicamente, no pueda ocurrir en función de las necesidades. Conmigo, va a ser siempre un segundo delantero. Es un jugador con grandes capacidades de finalización y creación”. Dicho y hecho. Titular en cuatro de los cinco partidos que ha disputado Portugal en esta Nations League, siempre ha ubicado a Joao Félix como ‘10’. Incluso, si esa decisión obligaba a sacrificar a un Bruno Fernandes al que, salvo en el choque contra Dinamarca en la ida en el que repartió dos asistencias, se ha visto obligado a actuar como falso extremo izquierdo. Un rol que el nuevo capitán de la ‘seleçao’ no tiene problema en asumir. “Si te fijas, yo rara vez estuve en banda. A la hora de defender sí, para seguir al lateral. Pero es la idea del míster: tener a alguien que juegue por dentro, que sea capaz de conectar el juego, bajar a recibir, servir de apoyo a los delanteros, creando un triángulo por el medio y por las bandas”. Joao Félix, motivado y crecido, ha respondido a esa confianza. De hecho, participó en, al menos, un gol en todos los partidos del parón de septiembre-octubre. No había motivos para no seguir apostando por esta propuesta. Sin embargo, en el ‘Día 1’ sin Cristiano, contra Dinamarca, nada salió como se esperaba y Portugal acabó encajando una dura derrota. La más grande desde 2018; la mayor en partido oficial desde 2014; y la más abultada de su historia en casa. Joao Félix, obviamente, no fue el único responsable de lo sucedido. De hecho, de las 27 acciones en las que entró en juego antes de ser reemplazado pasada la hora de encuentro salieron algunas de las pocas acciones clarividentes en ataque por parte de una Portugal inoperante. Ahí, estuvieron siempre atentos Höjbjerg y Hjulmand para no dejarle participar con comodidad recibiendo a su espalda: apenas ganó 1/4 duelos que disputó. “No conseguimos activarle entre líneas y ganar ventaja en el carril central. Dinamarca estuvo mejor y nos sorprendió”, señalaba Jorge Jesus después del choque. Habrá que ver si, después de lo sucedido en el Municipal de Braga, toma decisiones de cara al partido contra Gales en el que necesitan empatar para asegurarse el pase a cuartos de la Nations League. Lo que está claro es que, hasta el momento, le ha entregado las llaves de esta nueva Portugal a Joao Félix.

articles.title: Gruda, el ‘genio’ que ha conquistado a Klopp: “¡Fue una locura!”
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Leipzig, cedido por el Brighton, redondeó con un gol su debut con Alemania
articles.summary: El extremo del Leipzig, cedido por el Brighton, redondeó con un gol su debut con Alemania
articles.body: La banda derecha fue el gran ‘punto ciego’ de Alemania durante el pasado Mundial. La lesión de Lennart Karl trastocó los planes de un Julian Nagelsmann a quien se le criticó ferozmente por su reiterada apuesta por Sané. Con Brajan Gruda (Speyer, 2004), sin embargo, Klopp parece haber encontrado al ‘genio’ que cumple sus deseos. Su irrupción en el Mainz durante la temporada 23-24 —cuatro goles y tres asistencias— no le valió para ganarse un sitio en la Eurocopa… pero sí para firmar por el Brighton a cambio de 31.5 millones de euros. La mayor venta en la historia del conjunto alemán y el séptimo fichaje más caro de los ‘seagulls’. “Fue una situación dura para mí. Acababa de cumplir 20 años y me había acostumbrado a jugar en el primer equipo. Ahora, dejaría mi casa, mi familia, mis amigos y los entrenadores y compañeros que me habían ayudado hasta ese punto. Pero, cuando el Brighton me dijo que me querían, ¿cómo podía decir que no?”, explicaba en noviembre de 2024 en una entrevista con los medios del club. Recalaba en el mayor ‘trampolín’ de la Premier League y tenía en Hürzeler a un gran ‘aliado’. La adaptación, sin embargo, no siguió el curso que se esperaba. De hecho, contra los Wolves en la jornada 36, se le vio visiblemente emocionado tras salir como suplente y marcar el 2-0. Su primer gol de la temporada. Año y medio después, regresó a Alemania como cedido al Leipzig. “El club y el estilo de juego me convienen. Me siento bien aquí”, reconoció un Brajan Gruda que, con Diomande y Nusa adueñados de ambas bandas, mayoritariamente se desarrolló como ‘10’. Convenció, generando seis goles en los 14 partidos que disputó, y el Leipzig volvió a solicitar su cesión al Brighton… incluyendo una obligación de compra sujeta a condiciones cifrada en 25-30 millones. Ya sin Diomande, Demichelis lo ha reubicado en banda derecha. Es un perfil diferente al extremo costamarfileño del Real Madrid. Menos explosivo… pero más técnico, creativo y, sobre todo, asociativo en espacios reducidos. Ya ha producido siete goles en 13 partidos, superando sus registros del curso pasado. Es, además, el extremo que más regates completados promedia (5.72) en la Bundesliga. Ha vuelto a encontrar su sitio en Alemania y Klopp le premió convocándolo por primera vez con la Mannschaft de cara a este parón de octubre. “Juega en una posición en la que no tenemos 40 alternativas. Es un jugador con chispa y divertido. Todavía tiene mucho potencial por desarrollar. En el anterior parón estaba lesionado. Si no, ya habría sido convocado”, explicaba Klopp. Lo mandó directo al once contra Serbia… y maravilló. Arrancando desde banda derecha, intervino en 75 ocasiones; completó 40/47 pases; realizó 45 conducciones; y ejecutó 8/13 regates con éxito. “¡Fue una locura! El pobre lateral izquierdo…”, llegó a expresar Klopp. “Es un talento extraordinario. No voy a ser el diablo y prohibirle que regatee”. Muchos de esos regates llegaron cinco minutos después del descanso. Agarró la pelota en banda derecha a la altura del centro del campo, fue superando rivales en conducción y marcó el 0-3 con un disparo cruzado ajustado al poste desde la frontal. “Fue instinto. No pienso demasiado cuando estoy regateando. Solo lo hago. De todos modos, no creo que haya tiempo real para pensar. Simplemente sucede”, explicaba. “He estado sonriendo todo el tiempo. Era un sueño para mí y toda mi familia”, reconocía Gruda en zona mixta. A Klopp, desde luego, parece haberle solucionado un problema… mientras en el Leipzig se frotan las manos. Desde Alemania han empezado a informar que el Bayern lo tiene en su lista de fichajes futuribles.

articles.title: Veerman, el Xavi de Xavi recuperado del 'destierro': “Decidí apagar internet”
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista del Borussia Dortmund se ha erigido en el director de orquesta de Países Bajos tras ser apartado por Koeman
articles.summary: El centrocampista del Borussia Dortmund se ha erigido en el director de orquesta de Países Bajos tras ser apartado por Koeman
articles.body: La nueva Países Bajos de Xavi Hernández gusta… y se gusta. No ha tardado en dar con la tecla y todas las piezas parecen conectar a la perfección: Dumfries, Reijnders, Gakpo… Ahora bien, el encargado de conseguir articular todo el engranaje es Joey Veerman (Purmerend, 1998). La Eurocopa 2024 debió marcar su punto de explosión. Pero, después de firmar un curso notable con el PSV, fue ‘sacrificado’ por Ronald Koeman a raíz del debut contra Polonia tras haber arrancado formando trío en el centro del campo junto a Schouten y Reijnders. Fue suplente ante Francia y sustituido pasada la primera media hora frente a Austria tras errar 16/29 pases que intentó. No volvió al once en las eliminatorias. “Fue un momento doloroso para Veerman, pero creí que debía hacer un cambio. Le vi tropezarse con el balón… No puedo explicarlo”, justificaba Koeman. “Contra Polonia ya cometió errores, pero le quise dar una segunda oportunidad. Puede que sintiera la presión de los críticos que decían que tenía que demostrarlo también a nivel internacional”, reiteró tiempo más tarde en ‘Helden Magazine’. “Normalmente sí veo cosas. Pero, esta vez, decidí apagar internet”, reconoció Joey Veerman. Aquel debería haber sido el verano en el que, ya con 25 años, ‘volase’ del PSV… y quedó señalado. Koeman no le volvió a citar con Países Bajos y, por momentos, llegó a perder el sitio con Peter Bosz. Transmitía la sensación de haber salido del radar. Olé Book, sin embargo, lo reclutó para el Borussia Dortmund la pasada ventana estival por 22 millones. Titular en 11 de los 15 partidos que ha disputado, ha caído bien en una liga tan dinámica como la Bundesliga donde, por su perfil de centrocampista, existían dudas sobre su adaptación. “Aquí, se piden cosas que en los Países Bajos se piden menos. Eso ocurre a nivel de Champions o cuando juegas contra Ajax o Feyenoord. Pero en Alemania juegas un partido ‘top’ cada semana. Hasta ahora me está yendo bien”, expresaba en ‘De Telegraaf’. Es el mediocentro que ha registrado una menor punta de velocidad (29.2) en esta Bundesliga. Sufre en ritmos altos y a la hora de cubrir grandes distancias. Pero es un ‘metrónomo’ con balón: cuarto que más acciones progresivas promedia (14.4); el cuarto en pases largos completados (5.73); y el octavo en pases completados bajo presión (8.53) con una tasa de acierto del 100%. Uno de los grandes problemas de Países Bajos durante el Mundial fue la duplicación de roles en el centro del campo. Con De Jong y Gravenberch, sumando a Reijnders unos metros por delante, existía un exceso de conductores… pero faltaban pasadores. Xavi, sin embargo, recuperó a Veerman para la causa. Entró como suplente en el debut ante Alemania y, desde entonces, no ha vuelto a salir del once. Sólo en el segundo partido contra Serbia descansó durante la última media hora. “Creo que la conexión con Frenkie fue muy buena. Fluimos bien. Quizá, ahora se ha disipado un poco el debate. ¿Por qué dos chicos buenos con el balón no pueden jugar juntos?”, dijo después del último partido ante Grecia que acabó con 7-0. “Si no lo pruebas, nunca lo sabrás. Hoy ha sido la primera vez. Ambos sabemos que nos complementamos”. Su actuación, desde luego, volvió a ser excelsa. Fue el jugador que más balones tocó (114); el que registró más pases (88/95) con un 93% de acierto; el que más pases largos ejecutó (7/8); y el que más pases clave filtró (6). Asistió, además, a Reijnders en el 2-0 y desatascó el 4-0 del propio Reijnders y el 5-0 de Timber antes del descanso. “Técnicamente es ‘top’. Puede ser de gran valor para nosotros en nuestra construcción y en nuestra forma de jugar”, dijo Xavi cuando lo recuperó para su Países Bajos. Aun así, le pide más. “Con sus cualidades, no se puede permitir eso. Perdió dos o tres balones en la segunda parte. No puede pasar”, apuntó tras el partido contra Grecia. Es su extensión en el campo… y le exige como tal.

articles.title: Los posibles rivales de España: Francia, Portugal o Dinamarca y la ecuación a despejar con Xavi y Klopp como implicados
articles.standfirst: En el Grupo 2 de la Liga A podría haber un triple empate entre Países Bajos, Alemania y Grecia
articles.summary: En el Grupo 2 de la Liga A podría haber un triple empate entre Países Bajos, Alemania y Grecia
articles.body: La derrota por 2-3 frente a Inglaterra relega a España a la segunda plaza de su grupo en la UEFA Nations League. Este desenlace complica el camino de La Roja hacia la defensa del título en la fase final del torneo. Al no ser cabeza de serie, el combinado nacional será emparejado en el sorteo del viernes 20 (12.00 en Nyon) a un campeón de grupo en cuartos. La normativa de la UEFA impide que dos equipos del mismo sector vuelvan a verse las caras ahora. De este modo, el conjunto inglés queda automáticamente fuera de la ecuación para esta eliminatoria. El abanico de posibles adversarios se reduce exclusivamente a los ganadores de los grupos A1, A2 y A4. Francia es la única selección que ya tiene su nombre inscrito en ese bombo principal como campeona del grupo A1. El cuadro galo certificó su liderato matemático tras imponerse en su compromiso de la sexta jornada. Tampoco está cerrado el Grupo A4, que vivirá esta noche una auténtica final por el liderato. Portugal comanda la tabla con 12 puntos y parte como gran favorita para amarrar la primera posición. Le basta con empatar en su visita a Gales. Solo Dinamarca, segunda con 9 puntos, puede arrebatarle el privilegio si gana su partido a Noruega y los lusos caen derrotados. Mucho más abierta llega la resolución del Grupo A2, cuyo desenlace tendrá lugar este mismo lunes. Países Bajos lidera la clasificación con 11 puntos y depende de sí misma, aunque Grecia y Alemania mantienen vivas sus opciones de alcanzar el primer puesto Tras cinco fechas disputadas, Países Bajos es líder con 11 puntos de 15 posibles. Está invicta bajo la dirección de Xavi Hernández y vienen de cuajar una exhibición en el Johan Cruyff saldada con un 7-0 ante una Grecia que se mantiene segunda de grupo con ocho puntos igualada con Alemania, que hizo los deberes frente a Serbia a domicilio. La última jornada enfrentará a Alemania con Países Bajos y a Grecia con una Serbia ya matemáticamente descendida a la Liga B. Por tanto, cabe la posibilidad de que haya un triple empate a 11 puntos entre alemanes, neerlandeses y helenos. Para ello, Grecia debería ganarle a Serbia y Alemania a Países Bajos. "Siempre me ha encantado jugar contra equipos como éste, que también quieren jugar al fútbol. Esperemos que podamos frenar su juego y poder ser nosotros mismos", declaró Jürgen Klopp en la previa. "Jugamos contra Alemania. Es un momento para mostrar nuestro nivel, como hicimos contra Grecia. Significa mucho que volvamos a mostrar nuestra mejor cara", insistía Xavi Hernández. "No aceptaría el papel de favoritos solo porque nosotros tenemos 8 puntos y Serbia cero. Ante todo, Serbia no merecía estar a cero. Excepto en el partido contra Alemania, en todos los demás tuvieron sus momentos y sus ocasiones", apuntó Jovanovic, técnico de Grecia, quien reconoció que están "heridos" tras caer ante Países Bajos. Cabe recordar que el primer criterio de desempate en la Nations League atiende al enfrentamiento directo. Ahora bien, en caso de darse este triple empate, habría que atender al diferencial de goles... y ahí Grecia (-5) tiene muchas papeletas de quedarse fuera de acceder a los cuartos de final después de la goleada encajada el pasado viernes. Países Bajos, de este modo, tiene virtualmente asegurado el pase. Sólo una abultada derrota contra Alemania podría dejarle fuera. Mucho más interesante es la variedad de escenarios para los de Klopp. Serían líderes en caso de imponerse a una 'Oranje' a la que le tendrían ganado el enfrentamiento directo... siempre y cuando Grecia no gane a Serbia. Si Alemania pierde, estarían automáticamente fuera con independencia de lo que haga Grecia contra los de Paunovic porque tienen perdido el particular. El empate sólo le valdría a la 'Mannschaft' para avanzar como segundos de grupo si los helenos pierden ante Serbia. Más de uno, desde luego, estará con el transistor puesto en el banquillo y con la calculadora echando cuentas.

articles.title: 1 penalty saved, 3 stops, 100% run-outs: Man United keeper Senne Lammens regains form on international stage
articles.summary: Manchester United had two players in international action on Sunday evening in a busy night of Nations League action.Senne LammensThe Belgian Manchester Unit...
articles.body:
Manchester United had two players in international action on Sunday evening in a busy night of Nations League action.

The Belgian Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens has not had the best of seasons for Manchester United this year.

Nonetheless, he has had a consistent run in the national team owing to Thibaut Courtois taking a break from international football after the World Cup.

Lammens has been quite impressive in the group as his side finished second, one point behind France.

According to SofaScore, he made three saves in their impressive 4-1 win over Italy, including a penalty stop in additional time at the end of the match. It was a strong right-handed stop after guessing the right way, which will do his confidence the world of good.

Lammens also completed his only run-out, made a high claim and one punch to protect his goal.

The only blemish was his passing, as he completed just 59% of his passes and only 25% of his long-ball attempts.

Lammens also made a clearance and will hope to take this form into United's huge game against Liverpool on Sunday.

Tielemans also played in the centre of the park against the Italians and played the entire 90 minutes, as he did against Turkey.

He made two key passes and created one big chance in the match.

Tielemans also took care of the ball well, completing 91% of his passes, and had a shot on goal in the match.

Unusually, he didn't make any tackles or compete in any duels in the centre of the pitch, but he did make two clearances and blocked one shot defensively.

Finally, Leny Yoro was named on the bench for France in their 2-1 win over Turkey but did not get on the pitch.

articles.title: Dan Ballard’s Return Will Be A Godsend For Sunderland
articles.summary: Potentially having the NI international available during the hectic Christmas and New Year period could be crucial.
articles.body:
There's no doubt that prior to Sunderland's gutsy and potentially pivotal victory over Chelsea, something had been missing from the Lads' performances on too many occasions this season.

The narrow 1-0 home victory over the Blues hinted at something stirring within the ranks; something far more wholehearted and unified that had been on display during many of our previous fixtures, but as we edge nearer to — and let's be brutally honest here — an absolutely savage late November and December schedule, it really will be a case of "all hands on deck" as we aim to climb away from the relegation zone and ensure that Christmas is a time of renewed optimism in Sunderland circles.

With that in mind, one player's return to the fold — and with fingers crossed, his recovery is progressing well and he's edging ever nearer to a return — will be nothing short of a godsend for Régis Le Bris.

During the early weeks and months of 2026/2027, Sunderland's defensive woes have been a defining factor, with the likes of Omar Alderete and Kevin Danso periodically struggling for form and Nordi Mukiele occasionally having to hold the entire thing together through sheer force of will and supreme ability.

Hope that someone big, bad and "f***ing hard" is currently on the road to recovery, watching on from the outside and with a raging fire burning inside. Does such a player exist? You bet he does.

Dan Ballard is essentially Sunderland's answer to the former Leicester and England flanker Lewis Moody.

He's harder than that twenty year old pack of nails that remain unused in your utility drawer and he's wholehearted to the point of borderline recklessness. He's also utterly tireless in defence, a useful option at attacking set pieces and of course, the scorer of possibly the most iconic header netted by a Sunderland player since Niall Quinn against Newcastle in 2000.

Of course, the Northern Ireland international's injury record since his 2022 arrival at Sunderland would give even the most cheery club doctor palpitations.

Setbacks and knockbacks have been part and parcel of Ballard's Sunderland career and it's fair to say that he looked a little sluggish before his latest injury, but to my mind, he's already well on the way to becoming a modern great and his return to the fold can't come quickly enough.

Alderete, who's never looked quite right in terms of both form and fitness since returning from a gruelling World Cup, and Danso are by no means lost causes — far from it. They've got international and domestic experience to burn and will both have key roles to play at various stages this season but they need calming presences alongside them in order to thrive, and Mukiele and Ballard can fulfil those roles perfectly.

Ballard is the kind of player that, in the pursuit of victory, won't just make that extra tackle or extra block.

Instead, he'll make five tackles, three blocks and casually ask what all the fuss was about. He has form for returning from injury and slotting back in seamlessly — he did so during our 2024/2025 end-of-season run — and his no-frills approach is probably exactly what we need.

That's my kind of defender and given that Sunderland have looked far too ropey at the back for the bulk of the season, the thought of a fit, firing and freshly motivated Ballard returning to the backline and hopefully giving us some extra clout could be an ace card for Le Bris. He might have a little bit to prove in terms of fitness but in every other sense? No chance.

In four years at Sunderland (it feels like far more, given what he's seen and experienced since arriving on Wearside), few players have embodied the notion of "leaving it all on the pitch" to a greater degree than Ballard.

If one of those rolling skull-and-crossbones bombs from Crash Bandicoot was heading for your rowing boat, you'd want him aboard to cushion the impact of the detonation.

Likewise, if one of your main threats is from an aerially-strong centre forward, who better than him to win a couple of thunderous duels in order to set the tone for what's coming next? Climbing the table won't just require physical application — it'll demand 100% commitment from every player on the park and Ballard has undoubtedly become one of our true leaders in that sense.

Ballard proved his ability at Premier League level on multiple occasions last season — even if he didn't play what would've been a deserved role in our final-day victory over Chelsea. The next time his name appears on a Sunderland starting eleven, it'll be with a different degree of expectation, but one that he'll undoubtedly be ready for.

articles.title: Editorial: Another Huge Week For Sunderland
articles.summary: The Chelsea win offered some relief, but concerns remain over Sunderland's performances, injuries and Régis Le Bris. Can the Black Cats deliver another big r...
articles.body:
Once the nonsense of international football is out of the way, we can fully focus on what is going to be a huge game against Aston Villa at the weekend.

It's been a canny week away from it all, in all honesty. Usually, I dread the international break, but for some reason I haven't this time. Maybe it's the relief of finally winning a game, coupled with the fact we'd played nine matches inside a month. It's been a grueller, and we've been tremendously busy because of the sheer frequency of the fixtures. Whatever the reason, I think I've needed to switch off from it all (wey, to some extent).

Quite a few people noted that I wasn't my usual hyper self after we beat Chelsea. I think my confidence in the team took a massive knock after the defeat to Coventry, because that was such a huge missed opportunity. I also wasn't quite as excited as some were after we picked up those three points last weekend, because I didn't actually think we played particularly brilliantly – it was much improved in terms of the effort and application, but we did get lucky with a couple of big moments, and I reckon we should have conceded a penalty. Thankfully we didn't, and this conversation is completely different as a result, but a clean sheet and victory against one of the best teams in the league is a great start to what could be a much-needed resurgence.

The most important thing was that we won and, crucially, that our levels of effort were far better than they had been in the games beforehand. We got the job done. The speculation about our brilliant manager's future, which surely would have reached tipping point had the effort from the players been as crap as it was against Zagreb and Coventry, has calmed and he's bought himself some time.

That's not to say I wasn't chuffed, because I absolutely was, but I don't think we can ignore the start we've had to the season and pretend everything is suddenly fine. Many of the problems we've faced are still there, and there's a long way to go before I can properly breathe a sigh of relief.

Being in the dark about the injuries to Granit Xhaka and, in particular, Brian Brobbey hasn't helped either. Hopefully, Granit's problem isn't too serious and he'll be back soon, but I'm also excited by the prospect of Jules Ahoka finally getting a proper run in the team after the excellent start he's made here.

It's a lot to heap on such young shoulders, coming in for the captain at the base of the midfield, but he looks like he's got what it takes to play there. Nowt seems to faze him. I think we've come across a rare talent in Ahoka, and I have high hopes that he'll go on to enjoy a fantastic career. We may well look back in years to come and be proud that Sunderland played a part in his rise to the top. There's just something different about him, and he ticks an awful lot of boxes when it comes to becoming a top Premier League midfielder. It's early days, and I don't want to heap unnecessary pressure on him, but I trust my eyes and instincts with this lad. I'm absolutely gagging to see more.

We just have to pray that Brian Brobbey's problem isn't too serious. I was worried watching him in the second half against Chelsea because he was clearly knackered, yet continued to chase down long balls and put himself about. At the time, I put that down to tiredness, but we've got next to no insight into what the actual problem is. If we have to go to Villa without him, we're going to lose an awful lot. His presence, physicality and ability to lead the line are hugely important to this team.

I'm glad we've heard the players and manager talking about a 40-point target again, because it's clear that earlier in the season we'd lost sight of the important stuff. Perhaps we'd started getting carried away with where we sat in the league and what our position in the Premier League pecking order actually meant.

Villa represents another massive opportunity to go into a game as underdogs and pick up points that will help us move further away from danger. Equally, failing to get a good result will only see us fall further behind, and the fear of becoming embroiled in a relegation battle should be a huge motivator to go there and get the job done.

If we lose, which is entirely possible given how good Villa are, the pressure will be right back on. But what we cannot afford, regardless of whether we win, lose or draw, is to let our standards drop.

I think most of us will accept defeat if we feel the players have given everything and done as much as they possibly could to get a result. However, if the standards slip back to where they were against Brighton, Bournemouth and Coventry, the worry and panic will return, and the speculation surrounding Régis Le Bris' future will inevitably ramp up again.

I suppose that's the reality of Premier League management, though. You have to have the minerals to achieve great things at this level, and he's shown on plenty of occasions that he has them. I'm praying he can do it again, albeit in a new situation for us.

If he can, and if the players respond by producing a performance and result at the weekend, perhaps we can finally start looking ahead rather than constantly worrying about what's behind us.

articles.title: 'It's a massive win' - Declan Rice hails 10-man England for surviving Elliot Anderson red card to snap Spain's 43-game unbeaten run in Madrid
articles.summary: England midfielder Declan Rice has insisted the Three Lions were always confident of victory after holding on with 10 men to beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid on Sund...
articles.body:
England midfielder Declan Rice has insisted the Three Lions were always confident of victory after holding on with 10 men to beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid on Sunday. Thomas Tuchel's side overcame Elliot Anderson's second-half dismissal at the Metropolitano to end the hosts' 43-match unbeaten streak and top Nations League Group A3.

Visitors survive dramatic second-half dismissal

Rice and his team-mates delivered arguably the finest display of Tuchel's reign as Harry Kane's 15th international goal of 2026 opened the scoring before half-time. Quickfire strikes from Ezri Konsa and Ben White early in the second half stretched the lead to three. However, a slip-up from Jarell Quansah forced Anderson into a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal.

Midfielder praises squad's unwavering belief

Following the midfielder's dismissal, Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting spot-kick before Yamal set up Nico Williams to reduce the deficit to a single goal and spark a tense finale. Goalkeeper James Trafford produced a series of fine saves in the closing stages to preserve the advantage until the final whistle.

Speaking to ITV Sport , Rice revealed his team never doubted themselves: "We knew we were going to beat them. The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

"The first 10 minutes were the best we've played. Overall, 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against a team unbeaten in 43 is massive.

"Argentina that day [at the World Cup] wasn't meant to be. That's football. When they [Spain] got a second, maybe it could have gone another way.

Triumph in the Spanish capital saw the Three Lions record a 10th consecutive away win across all competitions , marking the first time in the nation's history they have achieved a 10-match winning sequence on their travels.

Furthermore, England's last two away meetings with La Roja have both ended in 3-2 victories, following their previous success in October 2018. That milestone makes England the first visiting nation to claim back-to-back wins in Spain since Yugoslavia managed three in a row in September 1988.

Sealing top spot in Group A3 ensures Tuchel's men will enter the Nations League quarter-final draw as a seeded nation alongside the tournament's other section winners. Surviving a ferocious late onslaught in Madrid will also bolster the squad's mentality following their painful World Cup exit against Argentina earlier this year. However, the coaching staff must plan without the suspended Anderson when the knockout stage begins.

articles.title: Morgan Rogers starts as England beat the World Champions
articles.summary: Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run is done
articles.body:
Morgan Rogers started while both sides fielded ex-Chelsea left backs in last night's Nations League encounter at the Metropolitano in Madrid. Neither of those is likely to be the most memorable story from England's impressive 3-2 win over the World Champions, but that's what shook out from the Chelsea filter.

It was in fact a direct matchup between Rogers and Marc Cucurella on England's right, while on the left flank, former Academy standout Lewis Hall was having a good old time running forward with the ball. That was a bit of a theme for the Three Lions, having a good old time — at least until Elliot Anderson's red card. Then it was shades of Mexico City, hanging on for the massive win. Thankfully, Jordan Henderson did not break his arm jumping over the advertising hoardings in celebration this time (probably because he wasn't there).

England, who came out with tremendous energy, built a scarcely believable three-nil lead at one point against the defending European and World Champions, with Harry Kane winning and scoring a penalty late in the first half, followed by a quickfire double from Ezri Konsa and Ben White as the game approached its hour mark. But then, Anderson made a very bad decision, giving away a penalty with a needless shirt-pull and getting sent off as well for not even attempting to play the ball, and from then on, it was hang-on time. Mikel Oyarzabal converted and Nico Williams scored just a few minutes after arriving on the scene to set up a grandstand finish. But we know how an inspired Tuchel team can rise to the occasion — even Rogers was defending! — and this was certainly a fine example of that.

With the win, England are in the Nations League quarterfinals. Morgan Rogers played the full 90; he had no further comments about the Cole Palmer situation.

Elsewhere, Roméo Lavia was back after sitting out Belgium's last game due to suspension, and played 76 minutes in their 4-1 win over Marco Palestra's Italy, 4-1. Mike Penders was an unused substitute as Belgium have now also qualified for the quarterfinals — finishing runners-up in their group to France, who beat Turkey, 2-1. Malo Gusto, after a performance that drew some rather terrible reviews last time out, was an unused substitute.

articles.title: Biggest winners, losers from Steelers' Week 10 blowout loss to Bengals
articles.summary: Here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from the Pittsburgh Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
Fans of the Pittsburgh Steelers may want to look away for this one, as, like the team's performance against the Cincinnati Bengals , this winners and losers list is going to be ugly.

We're doing things a little differently this time around, as our losers section deserves to be called out first, followed by a singular shared spot in the winners section. From a handful of duds responsible for an embarrassing performance on Sunday Night Football to two linebackers who weren't terrible in Week 10, here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss to the Bengals .

Don't let the garbage-time 143 yards and two touchdowns fool you, as Rodgers was abysmal in the Week 10 loss to the Bengals. He started the game 0-for-7, which included a near interception to Bengals safety Jordan Battle. The 42-year-old veteran quarterback finished the half with just 25 passing yards and zero touchdowns compared to Joe Burrow's 302 yards and three touchdowns. Rodgers didn't get much help from his playmakers, but this was by far Rodgers' most embarrassing performance this season.

Warren's hype train came to a crashing halt on Sunday Night Football, as the dynamic Steelers running back was held to just 15 rushing yards and 26 receiving yards. Warren struggled to get Pittsburgh's run game going and actually finished behind running backs Lew Nichols and Rico Dowdle in rushing yards. Warren's poor performance can easily be chalked up as an off night, as he was generating All-Pro buzz before this Week 10 lowlight.

Pittsburgh's offensive line, as a whole, was absolutely embarrassing. The unit struggled to protect Rodgers on key plays and failed to open up rushing lanes. Pittsburgh's offensive line was solid during the past four-game stretch but completely fell apart in Week 10. Mason McCormick's injury doesn't exactly instill confidence in the unit moving forward either.

Asante Samuel Jr. was absolutely outclassed in coverage against Bengals receivers on Sunday Night Football. Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and even Dohnte Meyers had a field day against Samuel. So much so that fans likely wouldn't be surprised if the Steelers decided to bench Samuel during the game. Samuel's struggles are a painful reminder that the Steelers traded away a top-10 corner in Joey Porter Jr. and failed to address the position at the NFL trade deadline. Omar Khan, you reap what you sow.

Honestly, if we could, there wouldn't be any winners for the Week 10 matchup. But to add at least something to the list, linebackers Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen are at the very least half winners in Pittsburgh's embarrassing blowout loss to the Bengals. Wilson and Queen combined for a ridiculous 33 total tackles and one sack. If there was any bright spot — and I'm not sure that there is — it would be Wilson and Queen on defense.

articles.title: Saints’ heartbreaking loss to Panthers on last play leaves Kellen Moore with regrets
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints have struggled mightily to find some consistency this year. The Saints have certainly had their moments. But as we saw on Sunday, New...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints have struggled mightily to find some consistency this year. The Saints have certainly had their moments . But as we saw on Sunday, New Orleans has also come up short on multiple occasions.

New Orleans was tied with the Carolina Panthers late in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Carolina had possession of the football, but needed a good chunk of yards to get in field goal range. A penalty on Kool-Aid McKinstry ensured the Panthers got those yards. And they went on to win the game on the ensuing field goal.

After the game, Saints coach Kellen Moore did not put blame on McKinstry for the loss. Instead, he focused on his shortcomings , especially offensive playcalling. "I got to call more aggressive," the Saints head coach said, via John Hendrix of New Orleans Football Network.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Saints did not have a great performance on the offensive side of the ball. New Orleans managed a little over 220 yards of offense in this game. Quarterback Tyler Shough threw an interception and did not throw a touchdown, either.

However, the defense certainly kept this team in the game. Even with the McKinstry penalty on the final drive, the defense played well. Linebacker Kaden Elliss showed out, recording 15 tackles, a sack, and two tackles for a loss.

The Saints will need to figure things out sooner rather than later. This loss sets them back in the NFC South race. But they remain alive nonetheless. New Orleans will take on the Chicago Bears next week on the road in Week 11.

articles.title: OK, then. Cincinnati Bengals might be Super Bowl contenders | Williams
articles.summary: Williams: The Bengals look like serious Super Bowl contenders after beatdown of Pittsburgh Steelers. Now can they sustain championship-caliber play?
articles.body:
Now then, that was championship-caliber football.

That was what the Cincinnati Bengals envisioned when they made all those offseason moves to upgrade their defense. That was what they expected from a healthy Joe Burrow.

Burrow throwing the ball to Ja'Marr Chase at will. The offense starting fast and never letting up. The rebuilt defensive line dominating from start to finish. The Bengals playing like a team truly hungry to deliver Cincinnati its first Lombardi Trophy.

Holy wow. Sunday night's performance was the type of beatdown that would make the late Paul Brown proud. It was over by halftime. The Bengals flat out embarrassed the esteemed Steelers in a first-place showdown in front of the Sunday Night Football audience. Let the good times roll.

How can you not consider the Bengals legitimate Super Bowl contenders after they played their most complete game of the season in their biggest game of 2026? The Bengals have performed well two weeks in a row, showing signs they may be able to sustain a high level of play down the stretch.

That was just plain fun, especially after there's been so much negativity around the Bengals franchise the past three seasons. From Burrow's multiple injuries to a plethora of whiffs on draft picks to poor tackling to not making the playoffs since 2022. Even in the week leading up to the primetime game, the Bengals embarrassed themselves by botching a deal at the trade deadline.

And the odds were against the Bengals seven days after playing in Spain. No team coming off an overseas trip had previously beaten an opponent coming off a bye week. The Steelers supposedly were well-rested for this AFC North battle. But they looked ill-prepared from the get-go.

Credit Bengals coach Zac Taylor, who should be coaching for his job in this championship-or-bust season . He was able to block out the distraction of the front office's botched trade. He was able to prepare his team to play with energy and purpose and show no signs of a letdown. The Bengals held the ball for all but one minute of the first quarter and went on to build a 17-0 lead with 5:28 left in first half.

It was one of the most impressive regular-season wins of Taylor's tenure with the Bengals.

"This is one of the better stretches we've had," said Taylor, in his eighth season. "This is the standard we've really expected for ourselves all along."

Most important, Bengals fans deserved this after what this franchise has put them through in recent seasons. They've stayed with this team, despite so many disappointments since the surprise run to the Super Bowl in the 2021 season. Paycor Stadium was packed to the canopies for a whiteout. Fans chanted "MVP!" after Burrow completed a 4-yard TD toss to Chase Brown in the third quarter. That gave the Bengals a 31-3 lead.

Things were going so well, in fact, the Bengals were able to put backup quarterback Joe Flacco into the game midway through the fourth quarter. That meant Burrow didn't even need a full game to throw for 409 yards and four TDs.

The Bengals made the Steelers' hard-nosed defense look like paper tigers out of the gate. Burrow was rarely pressured. Ja'Marr Chase, who had 231 receiving yards, was open all night. In the flat. Over the middle. Down the sideline. It didn't matter.

And the Bengals flustered Aaron Rodgers, who completed just four passes in the first half. The Steelers had 3 points at halftime, and they would've been shutout in the first half if not for a boneheaded taunting penalty on Bengals safety Jordan Battle.

Who saw this coming? Maybe no one except Burrow, who's been trying to establish a championship standard since the Bengals drafted him No. 1 overall in 2020. The Bengals are finally playing like Burrow has expected them to.

They're 7-2, riding a five-game winning streak and in control of their own destiny in the AFC North. The Bengals are tied for the second-best record in the AFC. They'd be the No. 4 seed in the playoffs if the season ended today.

Cincinnati just dominated one of the few playoff contenders left on a weak schedule. Kansas City (7-2) and Cleveland (6-4) are the only teams left on the Bengals' schedule that currently have a winning record. Forgive anyone around this title-starved town for thinking too far ahead. But leave it to Burrow to give us all a reality check.

"Nobody's winning championships in Week 9," Burrow said. "It's a big win, but we got a long way to go."

articles.title: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy drops cryptic upate on DeShon Elliott injury
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a lopsided loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football, and head coach Mike McCarthy did not offer many answers...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a lopsided loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football , and head coach Mike McCarthy did not offer many answers on DeShon Elliott's surprise absence afterward.

Elliott was a late scratch for the 38-18 defeat in Cincinnati after injuring his knee during pregame warmups . When asked about the safety's status after the game, McCarthy kept his update vague.

"During his warm-up, he had something that showed up," McCarthy said in a post-game press conference, via Chris Adamski of TribLive.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

It was a frustrating development for Elliott, who has been healthy for only two games this season and was expected to return to the lineup coming out of Pittsburgh's bye week.

Instead, he was ruled inactive shortly before kickoff. Pittsburgh was also without cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting, who was among the team's inactives.

The knee issue also brings back bad memories for the veteran defensive back. Last season, Elliott suffered a knee injury in a Sunday night loss to the Green Bay Packers that was expected to sideline him for the rest of the year, just months after he signed a two-year contract extension with the Steelers.

Without Elliott, Pittsburgh's secondary had no answers for Joe Burrow. The Bengals quarterback completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, two of which went to Chase Brown. Burrow threw three of those scores in the second quarter alone, sending Cincinnati into halftime with a 24-3 lead .

The Bengals piled up 484 total yards and built a 31-3 lead before the Steelers found the end zone.

Aaron Rodgers threw two late touchdown passes , one to DK Metcalf and the other to Pat Freiermuth, but the comeback attempt came far too late. Pittsburgh managed just 222 total yards.

The loss snapped Pittsburgh's four-game winning streak and dropped the Steelers to 6-3 on the season.

McCarthy and the Steelers will now await more clarity on Elliott's knee as they prepare to visit the Philadelphia Eagles next Sunday.
